records.text: Simple point: White now has a passed pawn. No enemy pawn is ahead on its file or either neighboring file.
Simple point: Black now has a passed pawn. No enemy pawn is ahead on its file or either neighboring file.
A different move would have made a passed pawn for White. No promise of promotion, but a real change in the pawn structure.
A different move would have made a passed pawn for Black. No promise of promotion, but a real change in the pawn structure.
White has an isolated pawn now. No White pawn stands on either neighboring file to support it.
Black has an isolated pawn now. No Black pawn stands on either neighboring file to support it.
Another move would have left White with an isolated pawn. No White pawn on the files beside it.
Another move would have left Black with an isolated pawn. No Black pawn on the files beside it.
Big picture: White has doubled pawns now. Pawns of the same color share a file.
Big picture: Black has doubled pawns now. Pawns of the same color share a file.
A different move would have doubled White's pawns. Same color, same file.
A different move would have doubled Black's pawns. Same color, same file.
White's rook has an open file now. No pawns of either color on that file. That is the change.
Black's rook has an open file now. No pawns of either color on that file. That is the change.
Another move would have given White's rook an open file. Empty of pawns, not necessarily empty of pieces.
Another move would have given Black's rook an open file. Empty of pawns, not necessarily empty of pieces.
White's rook is on a half-open file now. No White pawns there; Black still has pawns on it.
Black's rook is on a half-open file now. No Black pawns there; White still has pawns on it.
A different move would have put White's rook on a half-open file. No White pawns, but Black pawns remain.
A different move would have put Black's rook on a half-open file. No Black pawns, but White pawns remain.
White's knight has gained a defender. It had none before. Simple, useful thing to notice.
Black's knight has gained a defender. It had none before. Simple, useful thing to notice.
Simple point: White's bishop was undefended. Now something guards it.
Simple point: Black's bishop was undefended. Now something guards it.
White's rook has a guard now. That was missing before this move.
Black's rook has a guard now. That was missing before this move.
Big picture: White's queen is no longer undefended. This move adds a guard.
Big picture: Black's queen is no longer undefended. This move adds a guard.
A different move would have given White's knight the defender it lacked. That is the change to look at.
A different move would have given Black's knight the defender it lacked. That is the change to look at.
Another move would have put a guard on White's bishop, which had none.
Another move would have put a guard on Black's bishop, which had none.
White's rook had no defender. A different move would have supplied one.
Black's rook had no defender. A different move would have supplied one.
Simple point: another move would have given White's undefended queen a guard.
Simple point: another move would have given Black's undefended queen a guard.
White's knight has lost its last defender. Undefended does not mean lost.
Black's knight has lost its last defender. Undefended does not mean lost.
Simple problem: White's bishop has no guard now. It had protection before this move.
Simple problem: Black's bishop has no guard now. It had protection before this move.
White's rook has lost its cover. No defender remains; that alone does not prove a capture works.
Black's rook has lost its cover. No defender remains; that alone does not prove a capture works.
Big picture: White's queen was guarded. After this move, it is not.
Big picture: Black's queen was guarded. After this move, it is not.
Another move would have left White's knight with no defender. That is not the same as losing it.
Another move would have left Black's knight with no defender. That is not the same as losing it.
White's bishop would have lost its last guard after a different move. That needs noticing.
Black's bishop would have lost its last guard after a different move. That needs noticing.
A different move would have left White's rook unguarded. No defender, not necessarily a winning capture.
A different move would have left Black's rook unguarded. No defender, not necessarily a winning capture.
Simple point: another move would have removed the last defender of White's queen.
Simple point: another move would have removed the last defender of Black's queen.
Simple point: a knight leaves its original square. Its first move is made.
The knight was still at home. This move brings it out for the first time.
Big picture: a knight has begun its development, moving off its starting square.
A knight's first move. It is off its home square now. Start with that fact.
Simple point: a bishop leaves its original square. Its first move is made.
The bishop was still at home. This move brings it out for the first time.
Big picture: a bishop has begun its development, moving off its starting square.
A bishop's first move. It is off its home square now. Start with that fact.
Simple point: another move would have brought a knight off its original square for the first time.
A knight was still at home. A different move would have started its development.
The alternative would have been this knight's first move away from its starting square.
Big picture: a different move would have developed a knight. It had not left home yet.
Simple point: another move would have brought a bishop off its original square for the first time.
A bishop was still at home. A different move would have started its development.
The alternative would have been this bishop's first move away from its starting square.
Big picture: a different move would have developed a bishop. It had not left home yet.
Simple point: this move gives up some of what the better choice offered.
This costs something compared with the stronger move. It does not have to lose a piece to matter.
Big picture: a better move was available. This choice leaves a worse position than that choice would.
The position comes out worse than after the best move. That is the cost here.
Simple point: the other side can capture on the very next move.
The reply can take something straight away. Start there.
Big picture: a capture is available immediately for the other side. No waiting required.
There is something to take in reply. Whether taking pays off is a different question.
They made a mistake, and you used it. Good, solid response.
Simple point: your move makes their last mistake count.
The chance came from their last move. You took it. Strong.
There was a stronger move available here. Compare that choice.
The other move does better. Put it on the board and look at the difference.
A different move would have left a better position. That is worth checking.
The passed pawn moves forward. Less ground left to cover, but promotion is not settled.
Simple point: this pawn was already passed. Now it stands nearer the promotion rank.
Simple problem: the best reply attacks the king with check.
The strongest answer is a checking move. That puts the king first.
Good. You played the move this lesson asks for.
That matches the lesson. Keep going, steady as that.
The intended lesson move. Correct. Carry on.
Good. That move is right, but there is more puzzle left.
Correct so far. Work out the next puzzle move.
That part is solved. Stay with it; the puzzle continues.
Good. That is the move in your opening line.
The study line calls for that move. You have it.
Correct recall. That matches the opening you are practicing.
Simple point: the strongest move available. Best.
Best. The right choice in this position. Strong.
Good and sound. A stronger choice existed, but this one holds up.
A good move. Not the best available, but a solid choice.
